faq_heading: Surrey market stats: your questions answered

blocks.text: The boards report Surrey in 3 parts: Surrey (board area), North Surrey and Cloverdale. In October 2026, Cloverdale had the highest all-home benchmark at $930,600 and North Surrey the lowest at $637,000, a gap of $293,600. Over twelve months the three-part spread runs Surrey (board area) down 7.0%, North Surrey down 7.2%, Cloverdale down 4.6%.
Surrey (board area) benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical Surrey (board area) home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $899,900 in October 2026. That is little changed at −0.7% on the month, down 1.8% over three months, down 4.6% over six months and down 7.0% over the year. Over three years it is down 17.9%, and over five years down 13.6%.
The weakest one-year move in Surrey (board area) was for an apartment homes at −12.2%; the strongest was a townhouse at −4.5%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,288,000) and an apartment ($453,600) is $834,400, and a townhouse ($744,300) sits $290,700 above the apartment benchmark.
Against the Fraser Valley Board area, where the all-home benchmark was $860,000, Surrey (board area) is 4.6% above. Over the year the Fraser Valley Board area moved down 6.4% against down 7.0% here.
Of the 8 areas this board reports, Surrey (board area) ranks 5 by all-home benchmark, with Cloverdale above it at $930,600 and Mission below it at $787,800.

Detached homes in Surrey (board area): benchmark $1,288,000, little changed at −1.2% in a month, down 2.8% in three months, down 6.3% in six months, down 8.9% in a year, down 17.2% in three years and down 11.6% in five. That is 0.4% below the detached benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($1,293,800).

Townhouse homes in Surrey (board area): benchmark $744,300, little changed at −0.7% in a month, little changed at −1.2% in three months, down 3.1% in six months, down 4.5% in a year, down 12.1% in three years and little changed at −1.3% in five. That is 0.3% above the townhouse benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($742,300).

Apartment homes in Surrey (board area): benchmark $453,600, down 1.5% in a month, down 4.3% in three months, down 8.5% in six months, down 12.2% in a year, down 16.9% in three years and little changed at −0.3% in five. That is 1.6% below the apartment benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($460,800).

blocks.text: In dollars, the typical Surrey (board area) home is worth about $67,700 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $967,600. By type, detached homes lost about $125,800, from $1,413,800 to $1,288,000, townhouses lost about $35,100, from $779,400 to $744,300, and apartments lost about $63,000, from $516,600 to $453,600 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $943,300 six months ago and near $1,096,100 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $43,400 below the six-month mark and about $196,200 below the three-year mark. Against the Fraser Valley Board area, the Surrey (board area) benchmark is about $39,900 above the regional $860,000; a year earlier the difference was about $48,800 above.
Surrey sales at a glance, past 12 months

Over the past year, 946 Surrey houses sold at a median of $1.3M (middle half $1.1M to $1.53M), half of them within 33 days. 876 condos sold at a median of $435,000 (middle half $370,000 to $515,625), half within 30 days. Quarter by quarter, the median house price eased from $1.34M to $1.24M between November–January and August–October (196 and 246 sales).

blocks.text: North Surrey benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical North Surrey home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $637,000 in October 2026. That is little changed at −0.3% on the month, little changed at −1.2% over three months, down 4.0% over six months and down 7.2% over the year. Over three years it is down 19.4%, and over five years down 18.1%.
The weakest one-year move in North Surrey was for an apartment homes at −10.2%; the strongest was a townhouse at −3.4%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,254,500) and an apartment ($392,300) is $862,200, and a townhouse ($671,000) sits $278,700 above the apartment benchmark.
Against the Fraser Valley Board area, where the all-home benchmark was $860,000, North Surrey is 25.9% below. Over the year the Fraser Valley Board area moved down 6.4% against down 7.2% here.
Of the 8 areas this board reports, North Surrey ranks 8 by all-home benchmark, with Abbotsford above it at $702,800.

Detached homes in North Surrey: benchmark $1,254,500, little changed at +0.2% in a month, little changed at −0.8% in three months, down 4.3% in six months, down 9.8% in a year, down 15.0% in three years and down 11.9% in five. That is 3.0% below the detached benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($1,293,800).

Townhouse homes in North Surrey: benchmark $671,000, little changed at −1.4% in a month, down 2.2% in three months, down 4.6% in six months, down 3.4% in a year, down 14.5% in three years and little changed at +0.4% in five. That is 9.6% below the townhouse benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($742,300).

Apartment homes in North Surrey: benchmark $392,300, down 1.7% in a month, down 3.9% in three months, down 7.3% in six months, down 10.2% in a year, down 20.0% in three years and down 8.6% in five. That is 14.9% below the apartment benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($460,800).

blocks.text: Set against October 2025, North Surrey had 39 detached sales (33 a year earlier), 9 townhouse sales (15 a year earlier) and 52 apartment sales (77 a year earlier). Month-end active listings were 370 detached (about 439 a year earlier), 131 townhouse (about 134 a year earlier) and 656 apartment (about 731 a year earlier). Dividing sales by active listings gives a sales-to-active ratio of 10.5% for detached, 6.9% for townhouse and 7.9% for apartment.

In dollars, the typical North Surrey home is worth about $49,400 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $686,400. By type, detached homes lost about $136,300, from $1,390,800 to $1,254,500, townhouses lost about $23,600, from $694,600 to $671,000, and apartments lost about $44,600, from $436,900 to $392,300 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $663,500 six months ago and near $790,300 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $26,500 below the six-month mark and about $153,300 below the three-year mark. Against the Fraser Valley Board area, the North Surrey benchmark is about $223,000 below the regional $860,000; a year earlier the difference was about $232,400 below.
Cloverdale at a glance, October 2026
Cloverdale had an all-home benchmark of $930,600 (down 4.6% over the year), with detached at $1,326,400, townhouses at $757,900 and apartments at $501,800.

What the Surrey figure is
The $899,900 Surrey (board area) figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Fraser Valley Real Estate Board for October 2026.

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Surrey?
faq.a: In October 2026, a typical Surrey (board area) home was $899,900, with detached at $1,288,000. In October 2026, a typical North Surrey home was $637,000, with detached at $1,254,500. In October 2026, a typical Cloverdale home was $930,600, with detached at $1,326,400.

faq.q: Are Surrey home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: Surrey (board area) is down 7.0% over twelve months and down 1.8% over three months. North Surrey is down 7.2% over twelve months and little changed at −1.2% over three months. Cloverdale is down 4.6% over twelve months and little changed at −1.1% over three months.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: How do I find out what my home is worth?
faq.a: Jared prepares a home evaluation from recent comparable sales and the condition of your home. Contact him on 604-928-1361 or through the form on this site to arrange one.
